page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.metal-32xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6455B processors. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The CPU architecture is x86_64, incorporating advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU and memory performance. The server achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 22175.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 117766.74, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 480.81 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 213.95 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database performance is also notable, with Redis SET operations executing at 155.31 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 36342.33.

The server does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be handled via network-attached options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps. The absence of local storage and GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, positioning this bare-metal instance specifically for workloads that rely on external storage architectures and high-performance CPU-bound processing rather than local disk I/O or hardware-accelerated graphics.

Given its high memory capacity, fast DDR5 memory bandwidth, and dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon cores, the r7iz.metal-32xl is optimized for memory-intensive and compute-heavy enterprise workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal allocation of 128 dedicated vCPUs and 1 TB of RAM provides a dense consolidation platform for enterprise applications, offsetting the lack of local storage through high-speed network throughput and top-tier processing capabilities.
